title: "Objectives & prerequisites"
description: "What Hello Pico on Home Assistant teaches and what you need before starting."

## Learning objectives

::: {.callout-note title="Learning objectives"}
- Explain, using Phase 7 vocabulary, why Home Assistant is a
  **ControlSurface** and not a runtime, ontology owner, or a bypass
  around Kubernetes, Manifold, Wrangler, or the Python CLI.
- Merge a small Home Assistant configuration snippet that adds
  exactly one observation surface (a `command_line` sensor) and one
  safe control action (a `shell_command` fired by an `input_button`).
- Route every Home Assistant read and write through the approved
  `pico runtime` Python CLI ControlSurface so the graphical UI
  cannot drift from the declared runtime truth.
- Observe the same one-event / one-response contract the underlying
  [Hello Pico on Manifold lab](../hello-pico-on-manifold/index.qmd)
  proves, but this time triggered from a UI button in Home Assistant.
:::

## Prerequisites

::: {.callout-note title="Prerequisites"}
- Completion of the
  [Hello Pico on Manifold lab](../hello-pico-on-manifold/index.qmd)
  so a working `manifold` Namespace, `pico-engine` Pod, `hello`
  Channel Service, and topology ConfigMap all exist on your local
  minikube cluster. This lab observes and controls that runtime; it
  does not deploy it.
- Familiarity with the
  [`pico runtime` subcommands](../../bin/pico) — this lab wires
  Home Assistant directly to `pico runtime inspect` and
  `pico runtime emit`.
- A working Home Assistant installation (Container, Supervised, or
  Core all work; HA OS also works if you can install `pico` inside
  its container image). No specific HA version is pinned — Home
  Assistant's `command_line`, `shell_command`, `input_button`, and
  `automation` primitives are all stable and long-supported.
:::

## Environment

The Kubernetes side is unchanged from the underlying Manifold lab:

- Local minikube profile `manifold-lab` (from the
  [Kubernetes setup foundation](../../courses/kubernetes/index.html)).
- The `pico-engine` Pod is single-shot; if you already ran the
  Manifold lab to completion, delete and reapply
  `02-pico-engine.yaml` before this lab so the Pod is Ready again
  and can accept exactly one event.

Home Assistant-side additions:

- The `pico` executable from `bin/pico` in this repository must be on
  the `PATH` the Home Assistant container sees.
- A `kubeconfig` pointing at the same `manifold-lab` minikube profile
  must be reachable from inside the HA container (typically by
  mounting `~/.kube/config`).
- The helper script `hello-pico-ha-phase.sh` is expected at
  `/config/hello-pico/hello-pico-ha-phase.sh` inside the HA
  container. Any equivalent path works — just adjust the sensor
  `command:` in `configuration.yaml` to match.

See [`downloads/README.md`](downloads/README.md) for the operator
checklist that satisfies these three requirements.

## One-time setup (optional)

If you prefer to keep the HA integration completely isolated from
your host, run Home Assistant as a Docker container and mount both
the `pico` executable and your kubeconfig into it read-only. The
walkthrough is written to work regardless of which HA installation
shape you use, because the shape of the on-cluster runtime state
does not depend on how HA is packaged.
